items.claim: The single-verse cut at Jer.4.10 is warranted, but its stated grounds overreach: the verse is called self-contained and bracketed by third-person material on both sides, while the bytes carry a distinctive addressee run straight across the back seam into Jer.4.11 and turn to divine first person two verses on.
items.evidence: The cut itself holds at byte tier: וָאֹמַ֞ר אֲהָ֣הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.4.10 (byte tier), a speaker turn to direct address of the deity after the divine speech of Jer.4.9. What is undisclosed is the cohesion at the back seam. The three-word addressee run written לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם at oshb:Jer.4.10 (byte tier) recurs as לָֽעָם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם at oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier); the two spellings share one consonantal skeleton (skeleton grade), and that skeleton run occurs in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, 2 occurrences, MT keys) - these two adjacent verses and nowhere else. Both are governed by forms of the same speech verb: לֵאמֹ֔ר (oshb:Jer.4.10, byte tier) closes the reported false assurance, and the passive standing at the head of oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier) reopens it, so Jer.4.11 reads as a counter-report to the very speech-act protested here. A byte-true device on the seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and it is not disclosed. Second, the bracketing characterization is inexact on the following side: גַּם אֲנִ֛י אֲדַבֵּ֥ר (oshb:Jer.4.12, byte tier) is divine first person, as is the possessive of בַּת עַמִּ֑י (oshb:Jer.4.11, byte tier), so the material after the seam turns to divine first person within two verses of it. The parashah layer is reported correctly - the inventory carries no petuchah or setumah at MT 4:9 or MT 4:10 (single-witness; absence is not counterevidence).

items.claim: The distinctness argument for Jer.4.11-Jer.4.13 rests on contrast with Jer.4.10 and cites that verse as evidence, yet omits that the two verses carry both of the book's 2 attested occurrences of a three-word addressee run (sweep: 2 verses, MT keys), each governed by a form of the same speech verb.
items.evidence: The opening is byte-true: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא יֵאָמֵ֤ר stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier), and the temporal frame it uses is an attested shape in this book (sweep: 7 verses, MT keys), which supports holding the proposal at medium rather than higher. The defect is evidentiary omission on the seam the argument turns on. The addressee run לָֽעָם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִיר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם at oshb:Jer.4.11 (byte tier) answers לָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ וְלִירוּשָׁלִַ֣ם at oshb:Jer.4.10 (byte tier); one consonantal skeleton underlies both (skeleton grade) and it is attested in exactly two verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, 2 occurrences, MT keys), namely this seam pair. The link is not merely lexical: the preceding verse reports what was said to that addressee pair, closing on לֵאמֹ֔ר (oshb:Jer.4.10, byte tier), while this one opens by saying what will be said to the same pair, so the passive at Jer.4.11 inverts rather than departs from the preceding speech-act. Citing web:Jer.4.10 as the contrast while leaving the shared run unstated presents the seam as cleaner than the bytes make it. The claim that the wind image runs on to the outcry at Jer.4.13 is byte-supportable, and the parashah report is accurate: the inventory carries no mark at MT 4:10 through MT 4:13 (single-witness; absence is not counterevidence).

items.claim: The address unit Jer.4.14-Jer.4.18 is byte-warranted at both seams, sustains one second-person feminine addressee throughout, and its formula and parashah reports check out.
items.evidence: כַּבְּסִ֨י מֵרָעָ֤ה לִבֵּךְ֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם stands at the head of oshb:Jer.4.14 (byte tier): a second-person feminine singular imperative with the city named in the same clause, opening direct address after a seam that shares no skeleton token at all with the preceding verse (sweep: 0 shared tokens across Jer.4.13 and Jer.4.14). The address is sustained to the close in the bytes - the second-person feminine suffixes of the closing verse run to נָגַ֖ע עַד לִבֵּֽךְ (oshb:Jer.4.18, byte tier), which answers לִבֵּךְ֙ (oshb:Jer.4.14, byte tier), an internal envelope on the same noun that argues for this extent rather than against it. The postpositive formula נְאֻם יְהוָֽה sits verse-final at oshb:Jer.4.17 (byte tier) and is used here as closure of the embedded report rather than as the unit driver, which is the correct weight for a formula at this density. The mark report is exact against the inventory: MT 4:18 carries a setumah, the type is named correctly and not conflated with petuchah, single-witness and non-driving are both stated, and it is the span's sole mark (span mark count: 1, MT keys), so span symmetry is complete. One caveat that does not reach challenge: the label vocative-plus-imperative inverts the byte order, since the imperative is the first word and the vocative the fourth at oshb:Jer.4.14 - but both elements are present at the verse head in the Hebrew, so the argument does not depend on the English word order.

items.claim: The lament unit Jer.4.19-Jer.4.22 is byte-clean on its splices, handles the doubled ketiv/qere verse correctly, discloses both parashah marks in its span with the right types, and holds the speaker question at Jer.4.22 open on honest byte grounds.
items.evidence: מֵעַ֣י מֵעַ֨י stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.4.19 (byte tier), an outcry in the first person after the second-person feminine address that closes at Jer.4.18. The ketiv/qere handling is verifiable and right: the inventory records two variant notes at MT 4:19, matching the doubled-note count stated, and the splice occupies the first two words while the first ketiv, written אחולה unpointed in the source (source-byte quotation of an unpointed reading), is the third word - so the splice does indeed fall before either note, as claimed. At the far end כִּ֣י אֱוִ֣יל עַמִּ֗י opens oshb:Jer.4.22 (byte tier) with no speech formula of any kind at its head, which is exactly why the speaker of that verse cannot be settled from the bytes; holding it open with a frontier flag at medium_low, rather than asserting a speaker, is the proportionate posture, and no morphology layer exists that could decide it. Mark disclosure is complete and correctly typed against the inventory: setumah at MT 4:18 on the front seam and setumah at MT 4:21 inside the span, both named as setumah, both single-witness and non-driving, and the span carries no further mark (span mark count: 1, MT keys). The back seam is clean in the bytes as well (sweep: 0 shared skeleton tokens across Jer.4.22 and Jer.4.23).

items.claim: The four-fold seeing anaphora at Jer.4.23-Jer.4.26 is byte-true in every particular - all four tokens verse-initial, all four splices at byte tier, gloss extent matching splice extent - and the sweep places it as much the longest consecutive run of that form in the book, 4 verses of the 10 attested.
items.evidence: The four forms רָאִ֨יתִי֙ at oshb:Jer.4.23, רָאִ֨יתִי֙ at oshb:Jer.4.24, רָאִ֕יתִי at oshb:Jer.4.25 and רָאִ֕יתִי at oshb:Jer.4.26 each stand as the first word of their verse (byte tier at all four refs, verse-initial position verified against the source token order). The form is attested in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, MT keys), which fall into 6 maximal consecutive blocks; Jer.4.23-Jer.4.26 is the longest at 4 verses, the next longest runs to 2 verses, and the other 4 blocks are isolated single verses (sweep: 6 blocks, MT keys). The nearest site outside this span lies whole chapters away, so the statement that the device is absent from the surrounding lament and oracle material holds on the sweep rather than on assertion - though a shorter 2-verse run exists elsewhere, so this is the longest such block rather than the lone one (sweep: 6 blocks, MT keys). Each of the four splices is matched by an English gloss of the same extent, which keeps quote and gloss in parity at every one. The parashah report is exact: MT 4:26 carries a setumah, correctly typed, single-witness and non-driving, and it is the span's sole mark (span mark count: 1, MT keys). The unit_type deviation is disclosed on its face rather than left implicit - the proposal states why this is not classified as a vision report and confines the anaphora to texture rather than promoting it to a type driver, which is the right handling given that the seeing formula here carries no question-and-answer exchange in the bytes.

items.claim: Two defects in the grounds for Jer.4.27-Jer.4.31: the markedness asserted for the pronoun at Jer.4.30 is attached to the quoted qere when the consonantal divergence belongs to the ketiv the proposal sets aside, and the first-person turn at Jer.4.31 goes unaddressed in a rationale that enumerates why the other interior verses open nothing.
items.evidence: The onset is sound and is not what is challenged: כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.4.27 (byte tier), an attested onset shape in this book (sweep: 29 verses, MT keys), and the frame owner does change across the seam, from the prophet's first-person seeing at Jer.4.26 to the deity's own first person at דִבַּ֨רְתִּי֙ זַמֹּ֔תִי in oshb:Jer.4.28 (byte tier). First defect: at oshb:Jer.4.30 the inventory records 1 variant note (inventory: 1 note at MT 4:30), setting ketiv ואתי, unpointed in the source, against qere וְאַ֨תְּ (both quoted as source bytes; the pointed qere is byte tier). Consonantally the two readings diverge by one final yod, carried by the ketiv alone (verified by skeleton comparison of the two source forms; the ketiv is additionally unpointed, as the extract writes every ketiv). Token-bound, the ketiv skeleton is attested in 3 verses (sweep: 3 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:2 = WEB 9:3) against 110 verses for the qere skeleton (sweep: 110 verses, MT keys - a homograph-blended figure that is a floor on ordinariness, not a pronoun census). So the rare, divergent member is the ketiv that the proposal expressly sets aside, while the form it quotes and calls unusual and marked is the common one; neither witness marks it as unusual, WEB reading “You, when you are made desolate, what will you do?” (web:Jer.4.30). Second defect: the rationale states why neither Jer.4.29 nor Jer.4.30 opens a fresh unit but is silent on Jer.4.31, which turns to the first person at כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי (oshb:Jer.4.31, byte tier) - the same kind of voice turn treated as unit-making at Jer.4.10, Jer.4.19 and Jer.5.3. That verse is also tied back past the front seam to Jer.4.19 by two shared objects. The first is a two-word sequence, written כִּ֣י ק֤וֹל (oshb:Jer.4.19, byte tier) and כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל (oshb:Jer.4.31, byte tier), one skeleton under both spellings (skeleton grade) and attested in 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:18 = WEB 9:19). The second is the noun נַפְשִׁ֔י (oshb:Jer.4.19, byte tier), answered by נַפְשִׁ֖י (oshb:Jer.4.31, byte tier), attested token-bound in 10 verses (sweep: 10 verses, MT keys). A byte-true bracket straddling the seam argues continuity unless disclosed, and it is not disclosed. The parashah reports are themselves correct: setumah at MT 4:26 on the front seam and petuchah at MT 4:31 on the closing verse, types not conflated, single-witness and non-driving stated, and no further mark in the span (span mark count: 1, MT keys).

items.claim: The imperative onset at Jer.5.1 and the close at Jer.5.2 are both byte-warranted, the frame owner of the imperative is recoverable from the same verse's bytes, and the front-seam parashah citation is correctly typed across the chapter boundary.
items.evidence: שׁוֹטְט֞וּ stands verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.1 (byte tier), a plural imperative opening a search summons. The mouth behind that imperative is fixed by the same verse rather than left floating: וְאֶסְלַ֖ח לָֽהּ at oshb:Jer.5.1 (byte tier) is first-person singular pardon, so the summons is the deity's own speech, which is the point that has to hold before an imperative can be read as a frame onset at all. The back seam is a genuine frame-owner change in the bytes, from that first person to the vocative address at יְהֹוָ֗ה, verse-initial at oshb:Jer.5.3 (byte tier). Disclosure checks out on both live layers: MT 4:31 carries a petuchah, correctly typed and named single-witness and non-driving, on the front seam across the chapter division; the inventory records no mark and no variant note anywhere in MT 5:1-5:2, the chapter's variant notes falling instead at MT 5:6, MT 5:7 and MT 5:24 (single-witness; absence is not counterevidence). Ordinary numbering governs throughout - Jer.4.31 through Jer.5.3 lie outside the book's one offset zone, so the coordinates read the same in both witnesses.

items.claim: The single-verse cut at Jer.5.3 stands on the bytes, but the English gloss offered for its splice drops the very vocative the argument rests on, and the front seam separates two of the book's four sites of the faithfulness noun without disclosing the link.
items.evidence: The boundary claim is byte-true: יְהֹוָ֗ה is the first word of oshb:Jer.5.3 (byte tier), a vocative turn to the deity, and the following verse opens וַאֲנִ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי at oshb:Jer.5.4 (byte tier), a first-person resumption - so both edges are marked in the Hebrew and the cut itself is not contested. First defect: quote and gloss are out of parity precisely on the load-bearing element. The splice runs יְהֹוָ֗ה עֵינֶיךָ֮ הֲל֣וֹא לֶאֱמוּנָה֒ at oshb:Jer.5.3 (byte tier), four words beginning with the vocative, but the English offered for it covers just the question that follows, whereas the staged WEB text reads “O Yahweh, don’t your eyes look on truth?” (web:Jer.5.3). The vocative on which the boundary claim rests is present in the Hebrew splice and absent from the English set beside it, so the gloss does not carry the extent of the splice it glosses. Second defect: the noun of faithfulness at יְהֹוָ֗ה עֵינֶיךָ֮ הֲל֣וֹא לֶאֱמוּנָה֒ (oshb:Jer.5.3, byte tier) answers מְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֱמוּנָ֑ה at oshb:Jer.5.1 (byte tier); on a substring sweep that skeleton is attested in 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, MT keys, one of them MT 9:2 = WEB 9:3), two of which are the verses on either side of this front seam. The proposal cites web:Jer.5.1-Jer.5.2 as its contrast while leaving that link unstated, and a byte-true tie across the seam argues continuity unless disclosed. Severity is held low because the frame-owner change at the seam is explicit in the bytes and the disclosure of the surrounding layers is otherwise accurate - the inventory carries no parashah mark and no variant note at MT 5:3 (single-witness; absence is not counterevidence).
